about_mission2: Aussie Lunchbox is built and run by one parent in Auckland, New Zealand — the same person behind Aussie Lunchbox — not a company or a team. Prices come from Woolworths Australia's online shop, and every menu is costed against them, so the numbers you see are ones the site actually records rather than estimates pulled from nowhere. faq_subtitle: Answers to the most common questions from Aussie parents using the planner.
faq_still_desc: Can't find the answer you're looking for? Send us a message — we'd love to help.
faq_a1: Yes! The core weekly planner — generating meal plans, viewing recipes, and downloading shopping lists — is completely free. We may introduce premium features in the future, but the essentials will always remain free.
faq_q2: How does the meal plan generator work?
faq_a2: The planner picks 5 lunch menus for the week from the recipe database. It prioritises variety across categories (Sandwich, Hot, Baking, Cold) and applies any allergy or dietary filters you've set. You can also add fridge leftovers or favourite ingredients to influence the selection. It is variety by category — it does not score a week for nutritional balance.
faq_q3: Can I filter for allergies or dietary requirements?
faq_a3: Yes. Before generating your plan you can select Nut Allergy, Dairy Allergy, Gluten Allergy, Egg Allergy, Sesame Allergy, Vegetarian and Vegan, in any combination. The planner excludes matching mains and snacks, and the shopping list is built only from what survives. The two are filtered on different evidence: mains on our own recipe tags; packaged snacks on the allergen declaration printed on the supermarket product we track; fresh fruit and vegetables, and the few snacks whose tracked product carries no declaration, on flags we set by hand. That is how Rice Wheels, a chicken-flavoured rice snack, is kept out of a dairy-free plan: nothing in the name suggests dairy, but the packet declares milk. Sesame is the exception for mains: there is no recipe tag for it, so a main is kept only if none of its ingredients' tracked products declares sesame, and unlabelled bread, pastry and spice ingredients are left out because we cannot check them. If nothing in a snack category qualifies, that slot is left empty rather than filled with something that does not.
faq_a4: Every recipe in our database is individually tagged and reviewed for allergens. That said, the products you buy at the supermarket may contain traces due to shared manufacturing lines, and formulations can change without notice. For any allergy — especially anaphylaxis-level — always read the product label, even on items you've bought before.
faq_q5: Where do the supermarket prices come from?
faq_a5: Prices come from Woolworths Australia's own online catalogue and are refreshed once a week, so they are a recent shelf price rather than a live one. Coles and ALDI are not included — we'd rather price one chain properly than three badly. Treat every figure as a planning guide; your local store may vary.
faq_a6: Calorie estimates are based on standard portion sizes and average nutritional values from generic food databases. They are rough estimates intended to give a ballpark idea of energy content — not a substitute for precise nutritional tracking. Actual calories will vary based on specific brands and portion sizes used.
faq_q7: Can I save or favourite meal plans?
faq_a7: An account is optional — everything on the planner works without one. You can generate a week, download the PDF and print the shopping list as a guest. If you do create an account (email and password; there is no Google or Facebook login), you can star favourite menus so they come up more often, and email a plan to yourself.
faq_q8: Can I download the shopping list?
faq_a8: Yes. Once your weekly plan is generated you can download it as a PDF. For each day it shows the lunch, its main ingredients, the estimated cost and an estimated calorie figure, followed by a shopping list grouped by category (Produce, Meat & Seafood, Dairy & Eggs, Bakery, etc.). The shopping list in the PDF has item names only — per-item prices are shown on the planner screen. With a free account you can also email the PDF to yourself.
faq_q9: Is the app suitable for schools with nut-free policies?
faq_a9: Yes. Enable the 'Nut Allergy' filter and the planner will only suggest nut-free menus, with nut-free snacks alongside them. All menus in our database are reviewed for nut content and packaged snacks are checked against the allergen declaration on the product we track; fresh fruit, vegetables and the few snacks without a declaration are flagged by hand. Cross-contamination warnings are not used to exclude items, so for a school with a strict nut-free policy, still read the packet before it goes in the bag.
faq_q10: What languages does the app support?
faq_a10: Three languages are supported right now: English, Korean (한국어), and Chinese (中文). Switch between them using the language toggle in the navigation bar.
faq_q11: Can I suggest new recipes or report an error?
faq_a11: Absolutely! We'd love your feedback. Use our Contact page to send us recipe suggestions, report incorrect allergy tags, or flag any issues. We review all submissions and update the database regularly.
faq_q12: How do I use the fridge leftovers feature?
faq_a12: In the Planner sidebar, you'll find a 'Fridge Leftovers' field. Type in an ingredient you already have (e.g., 'chicken', 'spinach'), and the planner will prioritise menus that use that ingredient. This helps reduce food waste and save money.
faq_q13: Does the app work on mobile?
faq_a13: The entire site is responsive. Generate plans, browse recipes, and download PDFs on any smartphone or tablet — no app install needed.
faq_a14: Supermarket prices are refreshed weekly — every chain column in the price index is read from that chain's own online shop in the same run. New recipes are added in batches rather than on a schedule: the database went from 63 to {menuCount} menus across July 2026 and has been at {menuCount} since. Corrections happen whenever something is found to be wrong — two gluten-free flags were fixed on 20 August 2026, for instance. If you notice a recipe that looks outdated or a price that seems wrong, please tell me via the Contact page.
faq_q15: How do I create my first weekly lunchbox plan?
faq_a15: Open the Planner page — no account required. On the left sidebar (or tap the filter icon on mobile), set any allergy filters your family needs, exclude ingredients your child won't eat, and optionally type a fridge leftover you'd like to use up. Press 'Generate Plan' and within about five seconds you'll see a complete Monday-to-Friday lunchbox schedule. Each day shows a main meal with ingredients, Woolworths price estimates, and a snack suggestion. From there you can download everything as a single PDF or email the shopping list to yourself. The whole process takes under sixty seconds.
faq_q16: Can I customise the generated plan after it's created?
faq_a16: Yes, one day at a time. Each day card has a 'Swap this day' button that replaces just that day's lunch and its snacks with another recipe that fits the same allergy, excluded-ingredient, prep-style and thermos filters the plan was made with and isn't already in that week; the day's cost, the week total and the shopping list update to match. If no other recipe fits, it says so and leaves the day as it is. To start over, Generate makes a fresh 5-day plan from {menuCount} recipes. Before you generate, you can steer the result: exclude ingredients you'd rather avoid, add something from the fridge in the 'Fridge Leftovers' field so meals using it are favoured, choose prep styles or thermos-friendly meals, and, with a free account, mark lunches you like as favourites so they come up more often.
faq_q17: Does the planner support multiple allergies at the same time?
faq_a17: Yes, absolutely. You can enable as many allergy filters as you need simultaneously. For example, if your child is both nut-free and dairy-free, select both filters and the planner will only suggest meals that are free of both allergens. All seven filters (nut, dairy, gluten, egg, sesame, vegetarian, vegan) can be combined in any combination. The planner will warn you if there are very few recipes available for your specific filter combination, so you'll know if you need to relax one of the restrictions to get a full 5-day plan.
faq_q18: How do you handle cross-contamination warnings?
faq_a18: Our recipes are tagged based on their listed ingredients — if a recipe doesn't contain nuts in its ingredient list, it's tagged as nut-free. However, we cannot account for cross-contamination that may occur during manufacturing of commercial products or in your own kitchen. For children with severe allergies (particularly anaphylaxis risk), we strongly recommend always checking the label of every product you purchase, even if you've bought it before, as manufacturers can change formulations and production lines. Our planner is a planning aid, not a medical device. For severe allergies, please consult your child's allergist or immunologist and inform the school directly.
faq_q19: Can I use the planner for a child with coeliac disease?
faq_a19: The Gluten-Free filter excludes recipes containing wheat, barley, rye, and non-certified oats — covering the primary gluten sources. Because coeliac disease demands zero tolerance for trace gluten, we recommend treating our filter as a starting point and always confirming that the brands you purchase carry a certified gluten-free label. Coeliac Australia (coeliac.org.au) publishes a regularly updated product directory that's worth bookmarking.
faq_q20: How can I reduce my weekly lunchbox budget?
faq_a20: A few things move the number more than the rest. First, protein is what drives a lunchbox budget — the single biggest line in a costed week is usually the meat, so a meat-free day or two saves more than trimming snacks. Second, check unit price rather than sticker price: a yoghurt pouch can cost two to three times the same yoghurt from a tub even when the pouch is on special. Third, use the planner's 'Fridge Leftovers' field so the week is built around what you already have.
faq_q21: Do the prices include sales or specials?
faq_a21: No — we use regular shelf prices from Woolworths, refreshed once a week. Weekly specials and Everyday Rewards or Flybuys discounts change too fast and vary by region, so we don't track them. The upside is that our figures are effectively a ceiling: you'll almost always spend less once you factor in current deals. Pro tip: open the Woolworths and Coles apps the night before your shop, compare what's on special, and tweak your plan accordingly.
faq_q22: Can I build a shopping list for two weeks at once?
faq_a22: The planner currently generates one week at a time. For a two-week shopping list, we recommend generating two separate plans and combining the shopping lists manually. Many parents find it useful to generate both weeks on Sunday, then buy the non-perishable items (canned goods, pasta, crackers, etc.) for both weeks at once, and pick up fresh items (bread, fruit, deli meats) at the start of each week. This approach reduces shopping trips while keeping ingredients fresh.
faq_q23: Does the planner check that meals are nutritionally balanced?
faq_a23: Every recipe is mapped to the five food groups in the Australian Dietary Guidelines (NHMRC) — grains, vegetables and legumes, fruit, lean protein, and dairy or alternatives. The generator distributes variety across these groups over five days so no single category dominates. Each lunch targets a protein source, a wholegrain or starchy component, and at least one fruit or vegetable serve. For children with clinical dietary needs, we always recommend working alongside an Accredited Practising Dietitian.
faq_q24: Are portion sizes appropriate for different age groups?
faq_a24: Our standard serve is sized for primary school children aged 5–12, and every cost elsewhere on this site — articles, the homepage and the price figures — is on that basis. In the planner you can change it under Portion size: Kindy (about ×{kindyFactor}), Primary (×{primaryFactor}), Years 7–8 (×{intermediateFactor}), Years 9–12 (×{collegeFactor}) or Adult (×{adultFactor}). The planner multiplies each ingredient's share of a pack — and so the cost and the calorie figure — by that ratio; the menus stay the same. The ratios come from average daily energy needs by age in the Nutrient Reference Values for Australia and New Zealand (NHMRC), so they are an estimate rather than a prescription, and single items like one egg or one yoghurt pot don't scale neatly. Children still vary a lot: if they consistently bring food home, reduce the portion; if they're hungry after school, add an extra component like a piece of fruit. The Kindy (under 5) option under Allergies / Restrictions is separate: it leaves out foods with a high choking risk for young children, and ticking it also sets Portion size to Kindy.
faq_q25: How do you calculate the nutritional information?
faq_a25: Our calorie figure is a rough estimate. For each ingredient we take a generic energy value per 100g and a typical portion weight and add them up; an ingredient we have no value for gets a small flat allowance. These are generic values, not figures from a named food composition database or from the labels of the products we price, so treat the number as a ballpark — it is not precise enough for clinical use. We do not calculate protein, sugar or other nutrients. Actual values will vary with the brands and quantities you use. For children with medical conditions that require precise nutritional tracking (such as diabetes), please use a clinical-grade food tracking tool and consult your healthcare provider.
faq_q26: Can I share my plan with my partner or co-parent?
faq_a26: Yes. The easiest way is to download the plan as a PDF and share it via email, a messaging app, or AirDrop. The PDF has the 5-day menu — each lunch with its main ingredients, estimated cost and calories — and the full shopping list, which covers what your partner needs for the shop. It does not include the recipe steps; open a lunch on the planner screen to see how to make it. With a free account you can also send the PDF to your own email address using the 'Email Plan' button and forward it from there. We're considering adding shared accounts for families, where both parents can access and edit the same plan — let us know via the Contact page if this would be useful for your family.
faq_q27: How do I report a bug or incorrect recipe?
faq_a27: Thanks for flagging it — accuracy matters to us. Visit the Contact page, choose 'Tech Help', and include the recipe name, what's wrong (wrong ingredient, allergy mis-tag, pricing issue, etc.), and your browser name and version if it's a technical glitch. A screenshot helps enormously. Allergy-related errors are prioritised and typically fixed within 48 hours; other corrections within a week.
faq_q28: Is my data secure? What do you store?
faq_a28: We take data security seriously. If you create an account, we store your email address and the recipes you mark as favourites, using Supabase (a SOC 2-compliant database platform). Your meal plans are not stored on our servers — the last plan you generated is kept only in your own browser. We do not store payment information, dietary health records, or any information about your children. Cookies are used to remember your preferences (such as language) and your sign-in session. Google Analytics 4 collects anonymous usage statistics (pages visited, session duration, device type) with IP anonymisation enabled, and it only loads if you accept cookies in the cookie banner. Google AdSense uses cookies to serve ads; you can turn off personalised ads in Google's Ads Settings. We never sell your personal data. For full details, see our Privacy Policy.
faq_q29: Can I use the planner offline?
faq_a29: You need an internet connection to generate a plan, because plans are built on our server. Prices are not fetched live: they come from a weekly Woolworths price table that is bundled with the site when it is published. Once you've generated a plan, you can download it as a PDF, which works fully offline. One way to use it: generate the plan when you have Wi-Fi, save the PDF to your phone's Files app, and refer to it through the week without a connection.
faq_q30: How often is the recipe database updated?
faq_a30: Woolworths prices refresh automatically once a week, so what you see is close to the current shelf price rather than an old estimate. Coles prices are not tracked yet — every figure on the site comes from Woolworths. New recipes go in as batches rather than on a schedule: the menu went from 43 to 63 over the first half of 2026, and I'd rather not promise a monthly number I don't hit. This is a solo project, so there's no test kitchen and no editorial team — just one parent, the supermarket website and the receipts.

planner_seo_title: Create Your Perfect Weekly School Lunch Plan
planner_seo_intro: Aussie Lunchbox is a free tool that builds a Monday-to-Friday school lunch plan for Australian families. Set your allergy filters, hit Generate, and within seconds you'll have five days of balanced meals — complete with recipes, nutritional estimates aligned to NHMRC guidelines, and a shopping list priced against current Woolworths prices. No sign-up required, no hidden fees. Just open the planner and get sorted.
planner_seo_step1_text: Select any allergy filters (nut-free, dairy-free, gluten-free, egg-free, sesame-free) or dietary preferences (vegetarian, vegan). You can also exclude specific ingredients your child dislikes and add fridge leftovers you'd like to use up.
planner_seo_step2_text: Click 'Generate Plan' and the planner assembles a five-day menu in seconds, varied across categories rather than scored for nutritional balance. Each day shows a main, snacks, the full ingredient list, the method, and the estimated cost worked out as a portion of each pack.
planner_seo_step3_text: Download your plan as a PDF, email it to yourself, or share it. The shopping list is grouped by aisle with Woolworths price estimates — ready to take to the supermarket.
planner_seo_allergy_p: Every meal plan is built around your family's dietary filters. The database of {menuCount} recipes is tagged for six filters — nut, dairy, gluten, egg, vegetarian and vegan — and a filtered plan only draws on recipes carrying that tag. A seventh filter, sesame, has no recipe tag: it is read from the allergen labels of the products behind each ingredient. The tag describes the recipe, not the packet: brands reformulate and shared production lines exist, so for a serious allergy the label on the product you buy is the thing that decides, not this filter. That is the same caution given on the FAQ and terms pages, and it is meant literally.
planner_seo_price_p: Every ingredient in your shopping list displays a Woolworths price, refreshed once a week. We show per-portion costs, not just packet prices, giving you a realistic view of what the week will actually cost. Across our menu set the median lunchbox comes to about $3.40 a day.
planner_seo_howto_name: How to Create a Weekly School Lunch Plan
planner_seo_howto_desc: Open Aussie Lunchbox, set your allergy and dietary filters, and generate a personalised 5-day school lunch roster with recipes, a categorised shopping list, and weekly-refreshed Woolworths prices.
home_guide_heading: Australian School Lunch Rules You Should Know
home_guide_rules_p1: Australian school food policies vary by state and even by individual school. Most primary schools enforce strict nut-free or nut-aware policies to protect children with anaphylaxis. This typically means no peanut butter, Nutella, satay sauce, or any products containing tree nuts. Some schools extend bans to sesame seeds and kiwi fruit. Always check your school's specific policy at enrolment and again at the start of each year — policies can change.
home_guide_rules_p2: The 'Nude Food' or 'Waste-Free' movement is widespread across Australian schools, encouraging families to pack lunches without disposable packaging. Use reusable containers, beeswax wraps, and silicone bags instead of cling film and zip-lock bags. Many schools also restrict sugary drinks — water bottles are expected in most classrooms. Aussie Lunchbox plans naturally align with these policies: meals focus on whole foods, minimal packaging, and no high-sugar processed snacks.
home_guide_seasonal_h: Seasonal Meal Planning for Australian School Terms
home_guide_seasonal_p1: Most Australian schools run from late January or early February to mid-December, split into four terms with breaks between them; exact dates differ by state. Because Australia is in the southern hemisphere, Term 1 starts in summer heat and Term 3 falls in winter — which changes what you can pack safely.
home_guide_term1_desc: Summer/autumn — focus on cold lunches, fresh salads, rice paper rolls. Keep an ice pack in every lunchbox.
home_guide_term2_desc: Autumn into winter — perfect for thermos meals like soup, pasta, fried rice. Warm comfort food keeps energy up.
home_guide_term3_desc: Late winter/spring — transition meals. Wraps and scrolls work well as the weather slowly warms.
home_guide_term4_desc: Spring/summer — back to cold options. Sushi, sandwiches, and fruit-heavy boxes shine in the heat.
home_guide_nutrition_h: NHMRC Nutrition Guidelines for School-Age Children
home_guide_nutrition_p1: The National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) publishes the Australian Dietary Guidelines, which recommend that children aged 4-8 consume approximately 1,400-1,600 calories per day, and children aged 9-13 need 1,800-2,200 calories. A school lunch should provide roughly 25-30% of daily energy — that's 400-500 calories for younger children and 500-650 for older primary students.
home_guide_nutrition_p2: The guidelines recommend five food groups at every meal: grains (preferably wholegrain), vegetables and legumes, fruit, lean meats and alternatives, and dairy. A well-packed lunchbox should include a protein source (chicken, eggs, cheese, or legumes), a complex carbohydrate (wholemeal bread, pasta, or rice), at least one serve of vegetables, and a piece of fruit. Aussie Lunchbox calculates estimated nutrition for every generated meal plan — calories, protein, carbs, and fats — so you can verify your child is getting adequate fuel for the school day.
home_tips_heading: Make the Most of Aussie Lunchbox
home_tips_prep_p: A simple way to use Aussie Lunchbox is to generate your plan on Sunday evening. Open the planner, set any dietary filters, and hit Generate — you'll have a complete Monday-to-Friday plan in seconds. Use the shopping list for your grocery run, then spend 30–45 minutes prepping components that store well: wash and chop vegetables, cook a batch of pasta or rice, boil eggs, and portion out cheese and crackers. On weekday mornings, assembly is quick because everything is ready to go.
home_tips_combo_p: The blog has {posts} in-depth posts covering budget lunches, allergy-specific guides for nut-free, egg-free and multi-allergy families, and state-by-state canteen and lunchbox rules. There are {guides} longer reference guides alongside them. After generating your plan, browse related posts for prep tips, batch cooking and seasonal produce.
home_tips_allergy_h: Making the Most of Allergy Filters
home_tips_allergy_p: Aussie Lunchbox supports seven allergy and dietary filters: nut-free, dairy-free, gluten-free, egg-free, sesame-free, vegetarian, and vegan. You can combine multiple filters — for example, selecting both 'nut-free' and 'dairy-free' leaves out every meal and snack flagged for either. The Exclude Ingredients list goes further: tap an ingredient your child won't eat, such as Capsicum, and any meal or snack that lists it is left out of generated plans. The match is on the exact name in the list, so check near neighbours too — Avocado and Tuna/Chicken/Avocado are separate entries. You can also type a fridge leftover into the input field, and the planner will try to work it into the weekly plan to reduce food waste.
home_tips_price_p: Every ingredient in your shopping list shows a price sourced from Woolworths Australia's online shop. Prices marked 'Weekly' come from that online catalogue and are refreshed once a week, so treat them as a recent shelf price rather than a live one; prices marked 'Est.' are estimates used when an item couldn't be read. We also calculate a 'portion cost' — the actual amount of each ingredient you'll use per meal, not the full packet price. For example, a {cheesePack} block of cheese costs {cheesePackPrice} and covers about {cheeseServes} lunchboxes, so the portion cost shown next to cheese is {cheeseServe} — not {cheesePackPrice}.
planner_cost_basis: Estimated ingredient cost: every ingredient in the meal plus the snacks listed above, each costed as the share of a supermarket pack you'd actually use. It does not include a drink, or anything shown in the photo that isn't on the ingredient list. Photos are illustrative.
faq_q31: What exactly is included in the cost estimate?
faq_a31: Each day's figure covers every ingredient in the meal, plus the snacks listed on that card. Each ingredient is costed as the share of a supermarket pack you'd actually use — two slices from a loaf, not the whole loaf. It does not include a drink, or anything visible in a photo that isn't on the ingredient list; the photos are illustrative rather than a picture of the exact box. Prices come from Woolworths Australia and move week to week. In July 2026 we found and fixed a bug that had been mis-costing pack fractions, so figures published before then were unreliable — the numbers you see now are recalculated. Across our full menu set a box currently works out at a median of about {boxMedian}, ranging from roughly {boxFloor} to {boxCeiling} depending on the main.
faq_q32: Can I use these plans for my own lunch, not just the kids?
faq_a32: Yes. The menus are built around a school lunchbox, but none of them are only for children — they are ordinary meals in lunchbox form. If you are already making one, the simplest approach is a bigger portion of the same meal, drawn from the shopping list you already have. One thing to keep in mind: an adult portion will cost more than a child's. The planner's Portion size setting has an Adult option that scales each ingredient's share by about ×{adultFactor} — an estimate from average daily energy needs for adults compared with children aged 5–12, from the Nutrient Reference Values for Australia and New Zealand. The per-box costs elsewhere on the site are for a child's lunchbox. We would rather say that than let you plan a week's budget on a number that does not fit.
faq_q33: Can I use the planner for a kindy lunchbox?
faq_a33: Yes, with one setting. Tick Kindy (under 5) under Allergies / Restrictions before you generate a plan. The planner then leaves out the foods that New Zealand's Ministry of Health guidance on reducing food-related choking at early learning services says to exclude — for example dried fruit, popcorn, chips, hard rice crackers and sausages — and each day lists how to prepare the foods the guidance says to alter, such as grating raw apple or carrot, quartering grapes and cherry tomatoes, and chopping meat small. We also leave out roasted chickpeas; that one is our own call, not the guidance's. Ticking it also sets Portion size to Kindy, which scales the standard 5–12 serve to about ×{kindyFactor} — an estimate from average energy needs, which you can change. If your centre has its own food rules, follow those.

home_guide_nsw_desc: Healthy School Canteens Strategy uses a traffic-light system. Green = everyday foods, Amber = select carefully, Red = occasional only.

home_guide_wa_desc: Healthy Food and Drink in Public Schools policy mandates that 60% of food items sold must be 'green' category.
home_tips_seasonal_h: Plan Around the Australian School Calendar
home_tips_seasonal_p: Australia's school year runs from late January to mid-December across four terms. Term 1 (January-March) starts in peak summer — pack cold lunches with ice packs and avoid mayonnaise-based foods that spoil quickly. Term 2 (April-June) brings cooler weather — perfect for thermos soups, warm pasta, and baked goods. Term 3 (July-September) is winter in southern states but still mild up north — adjust your plans based on your location. Term 4 (October-December) heats up again as summer returns. Use Aussie Lunchbox's seasonal filters and blog guides to adapt your plans throughout the year.
home_tips_compare_h: How the prices on your list work
home_tips_compare_p: Every ingredient in your shopping list shows a price from Woolworths Australia, refreshed once a week rather than at the moment you look — treat it as a recent shelf price, not a live one. We show portion costs, the actual amount you'll use per meal, not the full packet price. Coles is not priced here: we'd rather track one chain properly than two badly. Tip: generate your plan on Thursday evening, when the new weekly specials drop.
home_tips_family_p: For multi-allergy households, stack allergy filters to accommodate different children simultaneously — the planner generates a single meal plan that's safe for everyone. For budget-conscious families, browse our Budget category blog posts for batch-cooking strategies and tips on making a whole chicken stretch across three days of lunches. For picky eaters, use the ingredient exclusion feature and gradually introduce one new food per week alongside familiar favourites. And for families with children at different schools with different policies, generate separate plans with different filter settings — it takes just 10 seconds per plan.
